purpose: Positive control for the SEMANTIC integration-failure class, with the pairs rebuilt so the consumer is inherited rather than written fresh. Both pairs are gold-validated on the harness-built images: clean merge, A passes alone, B passes alone, B fails merged. This run asks whether the harness detects that end to end when AGENTS write the patches.
pair_shape: A changes a provider's contract and ships its own tests. B extends a module that has depended on that contract since before either agent started, and is never told the contract exists. Neither agent opens the other's file.

tanstack_query_task/task1.cause: isStaleByTime negates timeUntilStale; !0 is true but !(-4000) is false once A stops clamping

zod_task/task1.cause: $ZodCheckMultipleOf tests floatSafeRemainder(...) === 0, which stops holding once A returns the raw difference

known_limitation: A alone is red on each repository's own full suite (query-core 7 of 683; zod 4 of 5366). These pairs reproduce the semantic class, not its stealth: a claim map is not the only way to catch them, since running the repo suite on A's branch would. See each task's SEED.md for why the shape entails this.
required_result: Both patches pass alone, merge clean, combined tests fail, and the pair's inherited edge recorded. If either is not detected end to end, STOP and report with transcripts; no further spend.
image_note: The two pairs live in different repos, so unlike s02 they cannot share an image. The disk guard keeps only the tags of the task about to run; both task Dockerfiles are rebuildable from the local base via scripts/build_task_image.sh, so a reclaim between episodes costs a rebuild (zod ~65s, query-core ~2min) and nothing else.
